[PREFERENCE] User is looking for tips on taking better black-and-white photos.  
[PREFERENCE] User wants to learn more about the best film to use and how to adjust for lighting conditions.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended films for black-and-white photography:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Ilford HP5 Plus 400: Classic, all-purpose film with wide exposure latitude.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Kodak Tri-X 400: High-contrast film with distinctive grain.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Agfa APX 400: Fine-grain film with neutral tone.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Fuji Neopan Acros 100: High-resolution film with wide tonal range.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested understanding the Sunny 16 Rule for exposure estimation.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested using the Zone System developed by Ansel Adams for controlling contrast.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Advised paying attention to lighting direction and shooting during the golden hour.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested using reflection and shade to add depth and interest to images.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended getting familiar with the camera's limitations and quirks.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested using a light meter for measuring light.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Advised experimenting with different development techniques for unique looks.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested scanning or printing negatives for best results.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Provided online resources:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. The Darkroom: Guide to film photography.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Film Photography Project: Podcast and community for film photography.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. YouTube Channels: Film Photography Tutorials, The Film Look, Analog Insights.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] Confirmed that Ilford HP5 Plus 400 is suitable for cityscapes at night due to its versatility and high ISO.
